text:
sara (Support): Hey team — customer Jane hitting intermittent 500s on POST /v1/batch. She gave one request_id: r-0a1b2c3d4e and said it happened around 2026-02-16T14:15Z. Can SRE lookup server logs and give repro guidance?

max (SRE): Thanks — I can look. Do we have region/cluster or node? Also ask Jane for any additional request_ids or a curl she used.

jane (Customer): Region is us-west-2. I only captured that one request_id. Payload is a 20-item batch; we can try to repro if you need it.

sara (Support): Posted the payload privately to Jane. Asking if SRE can run a request_id search in logs.

max (SRE): Quick search recipes below — we have logs in two places (live Loki index + archived ES). For recent hits (~last 7 days) try Loki:
```
{app="redwood-api", level=~"error|warn", request_id="r-0a1b2c3d4e"} | line_format "{{.ts}} {{.message}}" | sort by ts desc
```
If nothing shows, check ES archived index (older or cold storage):
```
POST /prod-logs-*/_search
{
  "query": {
    "term": { "request_id.keyword": "r-0a1b2c3d4e" }
  }
}
```
Note: logs roll to cold after 30d; hot retention is 14d for detailed traces. If the timestamp is older than hot window, we may see only sparse entries.

ingrid (Infra): Quick note: sampling is enabled on high-throughput routes — if requests >1000/s we sample non-5xx traces. 500s should still be in error logs but full span data might be sampled. Also our log indexer strips auth header values for PII — keep that in mind when asking for debug headers.

support-bot: 🔔 New ticket linked: TKT-4621 — assigned to max (SRE).

max (SRE): I'm running the Loki query now for the 14:00–14:20 window. If I find entries I'll paste snippets (redacted). If nothing, we should ask Jane to repro with an explicit X-Request-ID so we can correlate. Example curl to repro: 
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/batch" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d4e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"inputs": [...20 items...], "timeout_ms": 60000}'
```
Include exact timestamp when you run it.

jane (Customer): I can repro this afternoon and add the X-Request-ID header, thanks. Is there anything else you need from me?

max (SRE): If you can include a curl --trace-ascii or --verbose output file that would help. Also capture the response body and headers. If you see a stacktrace or internal error id in the response include that too.

sara (Support): I'll coordinate with Jane for a repro window (ETA 16:00 PST) and ask her to run the explicit curl. Also asking her to confirm token redaction is fine for debug bundle.

devops (Oncall): FYI, if this surfaces as a recurring pattern we should check the autoscaler / OOM events on the batch pods — they sometimes surface as 500s with no clear request_id attached. I'll look at kube events for the same timeframe.

max (SRE): Update: found two log lines for r-0a1b2c3d4e in Loki — they show a 502 from upstream transformer service followed by a handler panic in batch handler. Pasting redacted snippet: 
```
2026-02-16T14:15:12Z error request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e upstream=transformer-3 status=502 msg="upstream connection reset"
2026-02-16T14:15:12Z error request_id=r-0a1b2c3d4e handler=batch_process panic="nil pointer"
```
Looks like transient upstream failure + a nil check bug. I'll open an infra issue and tag the transformer team.

ingrid (Infra): If we need deeper traces and the hot trace window is expired, we can request a debug bundle from the node (requires customer consent). Steps I use: SSH to node -> /opt/redwood/bin/collect-debug --request-id r-0a1b2c3d4e --include-spans. Note this takes ~45s and is rate-limited.

sara (Support): Jane okayed debug bundle collection. I'll DM access scope.

max (SRE): Filed PR to add a nil check in batch handler, will push a canary. For now I'm adding a temporary fallback to return 503 instead of panic.

jane (Customer): Did the repro with header at 16:00 PST, request_id r-8f9e7d6c5b, attached verbose output in the private DM.

max (SRE): Found r-8f9e7d6c5b in logs too — same pattern. I'll follow up in TKT-4621 with root cause timeline and patch ETA. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sara (Support): Closing loop with customer and moving ticket to monitoring.

support-bot: Ticket TKT-4621 status -> monitoring
